newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BORDEAUX COACH SAYS REFEREEING OUT OF DATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BORDEAUX COACH SAYS REFEREEING OUT OF DATE.

text.p: Bordeaux coach Rolland Courbis has criticised how matches are currently refereed after an injury time penalty ended his side's unbeaten record in the French league.
"The problem this evening is not that of a referee, but a system of refereeing no longer in touch with the time in which we are living," Courbis said after Bordeaux's 2-1 home defeat by Strasbourg.

"To see in front, see behind you, see the sides, see the ball at the point of departure, whether a back pass is voluntary or not, it's too much for only one man," said Courbis, whose side conceded an equaliser at a corner he believed was wrongly awarded.
"We must move in France, 20 months before the World Cup, to try to get things changed -- before something serious happens in the stadiums."
Bordeaux, third in the standings, were incenced by the five minutes of injury time the referee added and defender Patrick Colleter was sent off for kicking an opponent in frustration.
"If we could introduce a fourth official, I think that would be a big step forward," Courbis said. "We wouldn't eliminate all the refereeing mistakes but we'd get rid of some."
Courbis's comments follow those made in England this week concerning criticisms of referees who apply the letter of the law rather than the spirit of the law.

At a recent public debate in London, semior UEFA officials said that introducing modern technology to aid referees could be considered fopr debate by the Task 2000 study group looking at the future of the game.
